source.title: Private Stochastic Non-Convex Optimization: Adaptive Algorithms and Tighter Generalization Bounds
source.authors: Yingxue Zhou; Xiang-Yi Chen; Ming-Yi Hong; Zhiwei Steven Wu; Arindam Banerjee

record.tranche_reason: Compares differentially private adaptive optimizers with DP SGD on MNIST, extending the optimizer generalization comparison to a private training setting.
record.gate_note: The paper also gives theoretical population-gradient bounds and empirical-gradient bounds; these do not directly test the listed claim versions. Figure 1 compares training and test accuracy for DP Adam, DP RMSprop, and DP SGD at three privacy levels.
record.test_reason: The study compares held-out MNIST accuracy across DP Adam, DP RMSprop and DP SGD under limited learning-rate tuning, testing V4 in a new, differentially private setting. It is not an original source for V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's empirical paraphrase is accurate: DP Adam and DP RMSprop tend to outperform DP SGD on the MNIST task considered. The authors also conclude that their privacy-based analysis yields a sharper population-gradient bound than the prior uniform-convergence approach.
record.recipe_differences: Differentially private gradient updates with Gaussian noise and gradient clipping; the experiment compares DP Adam and DP RMSprop with DP SGD.
record.method_sensitivity: Privacy level ε is varied; the authors say the adaptive-method advantage is especially pronounced at ε = 0.28.

fits_no_version.finding: Adaptive private methods also achieve higher training accuracy than DP SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the tested private MNIST recipe, DP Adam and DP RMSprop optimize training accuracy more effectively than DP SGD.

fits_no_version.finding: The theoretical analyses bound population and empirical gradient norms and improve dimension dependence over a prior population-gradient bound.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Differential privacy can yield sharper population-stationarity guarantees than the analyzed uniform-convergence approach.

record.problems: Empirical comparison is limited to fully connected networks on MNIST. Accuracy values are presented in figures without transcribed numerical values; results are averaged over 5 runs.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Non-private training, momentum SGD, language benchmarks, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay and switching from Adam to SGD.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations to large batches.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Learning rates are searched over {0.1, 0.01, 0.001}, decayed tenfold every 30 epochs, and selected by lowest final training loss. Batch size is 128; clipping is 1.0; δ = 10^-5. Results summarize five runs. The supplied text contains figure captions but no readable curves or numerical accuracies, so directions rely on the authors' explicit comparison; effect sizes and significance cannot be assessed. Despite the abstract mentioning two tasks, the supplied experiment section reports only MNIST.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Non-private optimizer comparisons, language benchmarks, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, and word-level language models.

relationships.condition: Differentially private MNIST training at ε = 0.28, 0.57 and 1.22, using a two-hidden-layer ReLU network and a fixed 100-epoch budget.
relationships.reason: The Figure 1 caption explicitly reports better test accuracy for DP Adam and DP RMSprop than DP SGD (R10–R18), especially at ε = 0.28; this qualifies extension of V4's non-private tendency to private training.
relationships.display_finding: Reported higher accuracy for both adaptive methods, especially at the strongest tested privacy level, remains unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.condition: DP optimizers on MNIST at ε = 0.28, 0.57, and 1.22
reader_labels.reason: In this private MNIST setting, DP Adam and DP RMSprop are described as having better held-out accuracy than DP SGD (R11–R12, R14–R15, R17–R18), so the non-private optimizer comparison does not transfer directly.
